roadmap_phase: Phase 1 (Safe Local Automation) -> Phase 2 (Agent Launcher MVP), MVP_ROADMAP.md
purpose: Define the MVP execution protocol for the future local Task MCP orchestrator: Codex submits prompts, MCP invokes available CLI/model runners, records completion, and returns artifacts for Codex review. This is a SPEC/GATE-DEFINITION deliverable (JSON policy artifact + JSONL rows + shell test) -- it patches NO source file, starts NO daemon, executes NO CLI runner, reads NO credential, and mutates NO task status.
consolidation_note: This protocol is NOT greenfield. A real MVP protocol already exists across agent_launcher_mvp_b02_v1, task_mcp_supervisor_loop_contract_b07_v1, task_mcp_supervisor_loop_status_tool_b08_v1, phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1, mcp_runner_topic_allowlist_design_b118_v1 (+ b119 enforcement), and mcp_codex_handoff_e2e_b116_v1. This artifact CONSOLIDATES that existing vocabulary (lifecycle states, error-taxonomy codes, adapter ids, safety boundaries) verbatim and adds only what those artifacts left unspecified end-to-end: a single tool-authority-tier taxonomy (24 tools, corrected to include the already-committed geoai_task_auto_pickup_dryrun), explicit timeout/concurrency rules referencing BOTH real timeout constants in the repo -- the b104 sandbox-ceiling bounded_timeout_seconds_default=3600s (not yet reachable, TIER_4-only) AND the currently-enforced core.py DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=60s subprocess bound (governs every live TIER_1/TIER_2 taskctl call today) -- and a merged review-handoff field list. It does not invent competing state/error vocabulary.

tool_authority_tiers.description: Every current or planned MCP tool/endpoint in this orchestrator belongs to exactly one of 4 authority tiers. Tier assignment is the mechanism that satisfies acceptance criterion 2 (separate read-only supervisor tools from write/execute tools), refined one level further: launch PLANNING is distinguished from launch EXECUTION, and execution remains entirely unimplemented.

execution_flow.description: One supervised loop = 4 legs, reused verbatim from task_mcp_supervisor_loop_contract_b07_v1.flow_legs. Only legs 1 and 4 are exercised for real today (TIER_1/TIER_3 read+plan calls); legs 2 and 3 are schema-reserved for the future TIER_4 gated launch executor.

legs.name: mcp_to_worker_cli_argv_handoff
legs.mechanism: NOT an MCP round-trip, NOT executed by this or any current task; would_run_argv is a template only. The existing worker protocol this WOULD reuse is exactly the loop this Claude worker session itself runs: python3 AITools/taskctl.py auto-pickup/brief/show/stage/guard-staged/review.
legs.causer: external: the worker itself running `taskctl review <task_id>`; MCP never causes this, only later observes it

legs.name: worker_cli_to_mcp_result_report
legs.produces: verdict in {pending, not_applicable_mvp} -- always one of these two today because no worker process was ever really launched by MCP
legs.lifecycle_transition: worker_review_ready (report only; no MCP-caused state change)

legs.name: mcp_to_codex_status_and_handoff
legs.mcp_tool: geoai_agent_task_status (dryrun projection) / geoai_supervisor_loop_status (B08 richer projection, pending wiring) / geoai_task_codex_handoff (B116, LIVE, implemented)
legs.produces: supervisor_state derived read-only from core._lifecycle_state via lifecycle_state_to_supervisor_state_mapping; never written back
legs.codex_action_after_receiving: python3 AITools/taskctl.py review <task_id> --runner <runner> (worker-side, already happened) followed by python3 AITools/taskctl.py done <task_id> (Codex-side finalize) -- both REAL, EXISTING, gated commands entirely outside this MCP contract's scope

planned.description: A dispatch request passed all preconditions but no audit entry has been written yet.

dispatched_dryrun.description: The dispatch plan's audit entry has been appended (decision=launch_planned, launch_enabled=false, launch_implemented=false). Ceiling state actually reachable end-to-end today.

worker_review_ready.description: The task card's OWN canonical status/worker_status (owned by AITools/taskdb.py) shows review/ready_for_review because a worker independently ran `taskctl review <task_id>`.

codex_reviewed.description: Codex has read a worker_review_ready task's status/result report and made a finalization decision. Records no new field on the task card itself.

blocked.description: Any error-taxonomy condition halted progression. Reachable from any other state. Never partially mutates the task card.

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: audit entry appended for the plan
external: worker runs `taskctl review <task_id>` on its own
codex reads leg-4 status and examines the report
error_taxonomy match at leg 1 (collision | runner_topic_mismatch | missing_artifact)
error_taxonomy match at leg 4 re-check (stale_task) OR timeout_rules.on_exceed (proposed, see timeout_rules)

lifecycle_state_to_supervisor_state_mapp.note: Reused verbatim from task_mcp_supervisor_loop_status_tool_b08_v1; read-only projection of core._lifecycle_state, never written back.

error_taxonomy.note: Frozen 5-code taxonomy reused verbatim from task_mcp_supervisor_loop_contract_b07_v1; this protocol adds no 6th code to the FROZEN set (see timeout_rules.on_exceed for a clearly-marked PROPOSED, not-yet-frozen extension).

collision.trigger: Two or more active task cards declare overlapping allowed_writes paths.

stale_task.trigger: Cached view of a task card no longer matches the LIVE card when re-checked (TOCTOU race).

runner_topic_mismatch.example_reason: one of: unknown_runner_topic_pair | malformed_runner:invalid_characters | malformed_topic:invalid_characters | action_not_allowed_for_runner_topic:<action> | per_wave_action_not_allowed:<action> | codex_action_not_allowed:<action>

missing_artifact.trigger: A path in read_first/allowed_writes does not exist on disk when preflighted.

failed_validation.trigger: A task card's validation command would exit nonzero when run by the worker.
failed_validation.notes: schema-reserved: dryrun-only mode always reports verdict=not_applicable_mvp, so this branch is never exercised end-to-end today

timeout_rules.source: phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1.sandbox.bounded_timeout_seconds_default -- the sandbox ceiling constant reserved for the future TIER_4 gated launch executor (leg 2, worker CHILD PROCESS bound). This is NOT the only timeout constant in this nested repo: see live_enforced_timeout_constant below for a second, real, CURRENTLY-ENFORCED timeout constant that already governs every TIER_1/TIER_2 taskctl subprocess call made today. An earlier revision of this artifact incorrectly asserted exclusivity for this constant (a false claim of exhaustive verification); corrected here to cite both constants.
timeout_rules.current_reachability: NOT reachable end-to-end today FOR LEG 2 SPECIFICALLY: leg 2 (mcp_to_worker_cli_argv_handoff) is never executed under this or any current contract (TIER_4 has zero implementing code; launch_queue_contract.py.attempt_start() always raises LaunchDisabledError). This protocol specifies the rule for the future TIER_4 gated launch executor; the 3600s bounded_timeout_seconds_default enforces nothing today. This does NOT mean no timeout is enforced anywhere in the system today -- see live_enforced_timeout_constant: a second, distinct, ACTIVE timeout already bounds every current TIER_1/TIER_2 subprocess call to taskctl.py.

live_enforced_timeout_constant.name: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
live_enforced_timeout_constant.source: tools/geoai-task-mcp/src/geoai_task_mcp/core.py:16 -- DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get('GEOAI_TASK_MCP_TIMEOUT', '60')), verified at git show HEAD:src/geoai_task_mcp/core.py (stable HEAD, not the dirty B11 tree)
live_enforced_timeout_constant.mechanism: core.run_taskctl(args, ..., timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) passes this value as the `timeout=` kwarg into the synchronous child-process call it makes for every 'python3 AITools/taskctl.py <args>' invocation the MCP server issues (Python subprocess module, run-and-wait style, argv-list form, non-shell invocation -- consistent with shell_execution_policy.no_shell_true above)
live_enforced_timeout_constant.scope: governs every currently-live TIER_1/TIER_2 tool call that shells out to taskctl.py, e.g. geoai_task_health, geoai_task_review_queue, geoai_task_list, geoai_task_show, geoai_task_pending_for_runner, geoai_task_auto_pickup, geoai_task_auto_pickup_dryrun, geoai_task_collision_guard, geoai_task_usage_report, geoai_task_export_jsonl, geoai_task_audit_log_read, geoai_task_mark_review, geoai_task_mark_done
live_enforced_timeout_constant.distinct_from_bounded_timeout_seconds_de: this is a SEPARATE, CURRENTLY-ACTIVE subprocess timeout for taskctl CLI calls (default 60s, applies today); bounded_timeout_seconds_default=3600 is a different, not-yet-reachable sandbox ceiling reserved for a future TIER_4 gated WORKER-PROCESS launch (leg 2). Neither constant governs or overrides the other; they bound different subprocess calls at different tiers.

per_adapter_note.claude_cli: future ceiling <= bounded_timeout_seconds_default; no override above ceiling permitted
per_adapter_note.deepseek_manual: not applicable -- human_in_the_loop=true, no local process to bound; a manual handoff would use a soft reminder, never a hard kill

timeout_rules.concurrency_rule: at most 1 concurrent gated launch per GEOAI_REPO cwd-pin at any time; over-cap requests are blocked (decision=launch_blocked_precondition_failed) and audited, never silently queued

on_exceed.status: PROPOSED extension, NOT part of the frozen 5-code error_taxonomy above -- flagged for owner sign-off before promotion so any future taxonomy bump is deliberate, never silent
on_exceed.proposed_action: the future TIER_4 executor kills the child process (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) and records this outcome; supervisor_state transitions dispatched_dryrun -> blocked, mirroring the existing dispatched_dryrun->blocked transition trigger set

credential_handling.detail: No code path in this protocol reads credential/secret env values or files. Reuses core.py's existing _sanitize_env_for_audit() pattern: only env var NAMES + set/unset boolean tokens may ever be logged (env_gate_status_tokens()), never values. env_scrub for a future TIER_4 launch passes only PYTHONPATH, GEOAI_REPO, PATH, and allowlisted GEOAI_TASK_MCP_* flag NAMES; all other env is dropped before any child process would see it.

shell_execution_policy.detail: would_run_argv is always an argv LIST, never a shell string; no future launcher may enable shell-mode invocation. command_allowlist restricts the only launchable binaries to 'claude' and 'codex' (deepseek_manual is manual_only, never a local process) plus exactly 7 python3 AITools/taskctl.py subcommands verified verbatim from phase2_orchestration_contract_b104_v1.command_allowlist: auto-pickup, contract, show, review, collision-guard, verify, usage. Anything else is blocked and audited -- no arbitrary command is ever prepared or run.

per_project_isolation.scope_today: single GEOAI_REPO cwd-pin per launch request + taskctl's own allowed_writes enforcement -- NOT a multi-repo/multi-tenant sandbox
per_project_isolation.non_goal_source: MVP_ROADMAP.md Non-goals: 'No central multi-project server yet.' and 'No rewrite of taskctl.py.'
per_project_isolation.mechanism: cwd is pinned to a single GEOAI_REPO value per request (parameterized repo root, not hardcoded per-tenant path); a launched worker (future TIER_4) would be confined to that one working tree; allowed_writes scoping is enforced by taskctl, not duplicated by the orchestrator
per_project_isolation.known_gap_flagged: core.py:13 DEFAULT_REPO hardcodes an owner-specific fallback path (overridable via GEOAI_REPO env) per mvp_contract_audit_v1 finding F2 -- not submodule-neutral yet; tracked in this artifact's next_wave, not fixed by this task

daemon_policy.detail: No new long-running process, listener, or background loop. The MCP server remains the existing stdio request/response FastMCP process; this protocol adds no additional daemon and no new server entrypoint.

network_policy.detail: Orchestrator opens no new listeners; a future launched worker (TIER_4) would inherit host network only, never a new orchestrator-managed socket/API call.

two_independent_gates: GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES (real, implemented, default '0', gates TIER_2 write tools)

GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_LAUNCH (proposed name only, referenced consistently across b02/b104/b118; LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED remains a Python constant False in launch_queue_contract.py so this flag currently gates nothing that exists)
write_gate_policy.additional_gate_for_task_mcp_topic: PER_WAVE_RUNNER_TOPIC_ALLOWLIST prefix check (core.check_runner_topic_allowlist), unchanged by this task

claude_cli.boundary: runs exactly one claimed task inside allowed_writes, runs validation, calls taskctl review, never finalizes done

codex_cli.boundary: orchestrator/reviewer/finalizer; a launched Codex WORKER instance must NOT self-review or finalize a task it executed -- separation of duties

deepseek_manual.boundary: no local process and no API key is ever held by the orchestrator; orchestrator only renders a handoff packet for a human to paste; returns to Codex review like any worker

review_handoff_contract.trigger: a worker task reaches taskctl review state
review_handoff_contract.separation_of_duties: the adapter that executed a task is never the adapter that reviews or finalizes it

review_handoff_contract.commit_hygiene_shape: {status: ok|warn, no_git_add_all: bool, mixed_task_commit_forbidden: bool, scoped_stage_only: bool}

known_exposure_gaps_for_next_wave.gap: No aggregated risk score across queue; human_brief.risk is optional text, not enumerated.
No per-task test-pass/fail state stored; verify is queue-wide, not per-task.

neural_bridge_note.doctrine: Per GeoAI neural-control-first doctrine, adapter/runner/topic SELECTION for a real future launch must be a LEARNED routing + abstain decision, never a regex/keyword cue router. This protocol adds NO cue router: the tool-authority tiers, lifecycle state machine, and error taxonomy are static, human-authored safety/interface boundaries (deterministic classifiers reused from core._lifecycle_state / core.check_runner_topic_allowlist), not a cognitive routing decision. Intelligence over which task/adapter/runner to dispatch remains deferred to the tracked migration below.
